# core


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A vault is one SQLite file that holds everything you have collected,
such as web pages, papers, talk transcripts, PDFs, notes and source
files. All of it is searchable together.
[`Vault()`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault)
opens the file `$VISHALAKSHI_VAULT` names, else
`~/.vishalakshi/vault.db`. `Vault(path)` opens or creates any other
file. `Vault(':memory:')` makes a vault that lasts only as long as the
process.

A [`Vault`](https://vedicreader.github.io/vishalakshi/core.html#vault)
is a [litesearch](https://github.com/Karthik777/litesearch) `Index`.
litesearch decides how text is stored and found. Each thing you add
becomes a document. litesearch splits a document along its headings into
a tree of sections, which it calls nodes. It cuts the text of each
section into chunks. It stores every chunk twice. One copy is text, for
the full-text keyword search of SQLite. The other copy is a vector, a
list of numbers from an embedding model. The model puts texts with
similar meanings near each other. A search runs both lookups and merges
the two rankings with reciprocal rank fusion (RRF). RRF scores each
chunk by its rank in each list. It does not use the raw scores, because
a keyword score and a vector distance cannot be compared. The default
embedding model is `potion-multilingual-128M`. It is small and fast and
covers over 100 languages, including Devanagari. `encoder=` picks
another model (see [concepts](07_concepts.ipynb)).

The vault adds these to litesearch:

- a `kind` on every document that says how it arrived (`web`, `pdf`,
  `arxiv`, `note`, `code` and so on)
- shelves that keep separate collections in the same file
- marks that record the judgements of a person about a document
- an entity graph and a topic map
- the methods on the other pages that fetch, read, extract and answer

### Vault.add

``` python
def add(
    src, # text, `[(page_no, text)]`, a file path, or a directory
    title:str=None, # document title; defaults to the filename, or the first line of text
    source:str=None, # url or path; defaults to the title. The document id is a hash of the source and the title
    kind:str=None, # one of KINDS: the facet you filter and report on
    meta:dict=None, # provenance: the query that found it, when, which tier fetched it
    force:bool=False, # re-ingest a source already present
    refresh:bool=True, # re-ingest text whose content hash differs from the filed hash. A file refreshes only through `force` or `housekeep`
    **kw
)->dict: # forwarded to litesearch add_doc (chunker, summarize, with_heading)
```

*Add text, pages, a file or a directory to the vault, adding a source
again only when its content changed.*

`search` returns chunks. Each hit has a short `snippet`, the `node_id`
of its section and the `doc_id` of its document. `sections` ranks whole
sections instead. `context` returns the text to give a language model.
It returns whole sections. Each section has a breadcrumb, the path of
headings down to it, such as `Attention › Multi-head`. Each section also
has a `node_id`, which `read` turns back into the full section. The
`related` list of `context` holds sections as leads. They are found by
vector similarity to the results, not by matching the question.
`context` also adds two sections from each other shelf (`shelves=2`). It
adds code sections (`code=`) when [kosha](03_code.ipynb) has indexed the
repository. `rerank=True` reorders the hits with a cross-encoder model.
It needs the `rerank` extra (`pip install 'vishalakshi[rerank]'`).

These methods, and `read` and `document`, take `pii=`. The default is
`off`. See [pii](09_pii.ipynb). Every row also has `age`, the seconds
since its document was filed, and `stale`. Stale rows sort last.


*Make a retrieval method take `pii=` and `pii_ner=` and apply that

A `node_id` names a section. A `doc_id` names a document. `doc(ref)`
finds the row of a document by its id, its exact source, or part of its
title. `document(ref)` rebuilds a whole document in reading order and
puts its headings back. A model reads this text to extract fields. Given
a path that the vault has never seen, `document` reads the file from
disk. `read(node_id)` rebuilds one section. `toc` returns the heading
tree of the shelf or of one document.

The `meta` of a document holds where it came from and anything set with
`set_meta`, such as its doctype. Adding a changed document again
rewrites its `meta`. A lasting judgement about a document goes in the
`doc_marks` table instead (see Marks below).

## Shelves

One vault file can hold several shelves. A shelf is a separate
collection with its own chunks, section tree and vector index. A large
corpus on one shelf, such as a thousand papers, does not crowd a small
shelf out of the rankings. `shelf(name)` opens a shelf and creates it
the first time. A shelf keeps the embedding model it was first written
with. Reopening it with a different model raises an error, because
vectors from two models cannot be compared. `shelves()` lists the
shelves with their models and document counts. `drop_shelf` deletes a
shelf. The main shelf is called `store`. `SHELVES` names the shelves
that the vault itself uses: `store`, `papers`, `sanskrit`, `code` and
`data`. Acquisition sends some kinds to their own shelf through
`KIND_SHELF`, below.

## Marks

A mark is a judgement about one document. The `doc_marks` table keeps it
when the document is added again. There are three marks. `noisy` is for
junk such as a cookie banner or a site footer. `search`, `sections`,
`context` and `ask` leave noisy documents out. `pii_override` holds the
privacy marks described on [pii](09_pii.ipynb). `stale` says that a
document no longer matches its source. Search still returns a stale
document, flagged and sorted last. The vault clears the mark when the
document is added again with new content. `mark` sets any of them.
`mark_noisy`, `mark_stale` and the pii methods are the named ways to set
a mark. `marks()` lists every mark on the shelf. `marks(ref)` returns
the mark on one document.

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    assert 'vault_stores' not in v.db.t                    # litesearch's store_meta is the one registry
    test_eq(v.db._store_meta('store')['encoder'], 'hash-256')
    assert v.shelves()[0]['store'] == 'store'
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'test.db'
    a = Vault(p, offline=True)
    a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    assert b.doc('report')
    test_eq(len(b.shelves()), 1)
    assert 'feedback' in b.db.t
    assert 'rankers' in b.db.t
```

``` python
# A vault written before litesearch stamped encoders carries only `vault_stores` rows.
# The vault copies each row into `store_meta` once, on first use. `shelf()` then reopens with the encoder that wrote it.
# Nothing writes `vault_stores` rows again.
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'old.db'
    a = Vault(p, offline=True); a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    a.shelf('papers', encoder='hash', dims=64).add('Paper about thorium.', title='paper')
    a.db.q('update store_meta set encoder=?', [''])
    a.db.t.vault_stores.create(store=str, encoder=str, dims=int, method=str, added_at=float, pk='store')
    a.db.t.vault_stores.insert_all([dict(store='store', encoder='hash', dims=256, method='hash', added_at=time.time()),
                                    dict(store='papers', encoder='hash', dims=64, method='hash', added_at=time.time())])
    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    test_eq(b.db._store_meta('store')['encoder'], 'hash-256')
    sh = b.shelf('papers')
    test_eq((sh.enc.method, sh.enc.dims, b.db._store_meta('papers')['encoder']), ('hash', 64, 'hash-64'))
    test_eq([s['dims'] for s in b.shelves()], [256, 64])
    test_fail(lambda: Vault(p, offline=True, store='papers'), contains='Two encoders')
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    p = Path(d)/'test.db'

    a = Vault(p, offline=True)
    a.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')
    before = list(a.marks())

    b = Vault(p, offline=True)
    assert list(b.marks()) == before
```

``` python
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.add('A report about polonium.', title='report')

    assert 'doc_marks' in v.db.t
    assert v.marks() == []

    v.mark('report', noisy=True)
    assert v.marks('report')['noisy'] == 1
    assert not v.search('polonium')
    assert v.search('polonium', include_noisy=True)
```

A shelf opened from a vault shares the embedding model of the vault in
memory. Opening many shelves loads the model once. `offline=True` and
`$VISHALAKSHI_OFFLINE` also carry over to a new shelf. An offline vault
never downloads a model.

``` python
# A shelf is a partition. It reuses the live encoder of the vault and does not load a second encoder.
from tempfile import mkdtemp

v = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'v.db')
s = v.shelf('project')
assert s.enc.model is v.enc.model      # the same object: a shelf per project used to cost a load each
assert s.name == 'project'

# `offline=True` has to survive into a brand-new shelf, or it does not mean "never download":
# a shelf with no registry row used to fall through to the default and load a real model
o = Vault(Path(mkdtemp())/'o.db', offline=True)
assert o.enc.method == 'hash' and o.shelf('fresh').enc.method == 'hash'

# An explicit encoder still wins, and a shelf already on disk is reopened with whatever wrote it.
r = v.shelf('papers', encoder='code')
assert r.enc.name == ENCODERS['code']
r.note('rank fusion needs only each leg ordering', title='RRF')
assert Vault(v.path).shelf('papers').enc.name == ENCODERS['code']
assert Vault(v.path).shelf('papers').search('rank fusion'), 'the reopened shelf lost its note'
print('shelf encoders:', {x['store']: x['encoder'] for x in v.shelves()})
```

`KIND_SHELF` sends documents of some kinds to their own shelf when they
are added to the main shelf. arXiv papers go to `papers`. Sanskrit files
go to `sanskrit` when `add_dir` finds them and ganapati is installed.
`search` and `sections` look at one shelf only. `context` adds results
from the other shelves (`shelves=`). `elsewhere(q)` searches every other
shelf directly. Use it when the answer can be on another shelf.

``` python
# a store of names (a graph's `entities` table) in store_meta is not a shelf: no query touches its missing docs table
with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.shelf('papers').add('A paper about polonium.', title='paper')
    v.db.q('create table entities (id text primary key, content text, embedding blob, metadata text, uploaded_at text, kind text, canon text, freq int)')
    v.db.q("insert into store_meta(name, encoder) values ('entities', '')")
    sql, ex = [], v.db.execute
    v.db.execute = lambda s, *a, **k: sql.append(s) or ex(s, *a, **k)
    test_eq(v.shelves().attrgot('store'), ['store', 'papers'])
    test_eq(v.elsewhere('polonium', shelves=['papers', 'entities']).attrgot('store').unique(), ['papers'])
    test_eq(len(v.elsewhere('polonium')), 1)
    del v.db.execute
    test_eq([s for s in sql if 'entities_docs' in s], [])

    v.db.q("delete from store_meta where name='entities'")
    test_fail(lambda: v.shelf('entities'), contains='no doc_id')
    test_eq(v.db.q("select name from store_meta where name='entities'"), [])

    old = os.environ.get('VISHALAKSHI_VAULT')
    os.environ['VISHALAKSHI_VAULT'] = str(Path(d)/'env.db')
    try: test_eq(Vault(offline=True).path, str(Path(d)/'env.db'))
    finally: os.environ.pop('VISHALAKSHI_VAULT') if old is None else os.environ.update(VISHALAKSHI_VAULT=old)
```

``` python
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

class _Chat:
    "A scripted extraction, so the graph is the same every run and no model is asked for."
    runtime = 'litert'   # it stands in for the local default; a hosted chat builds only over an all-Open shelf
    def oneshot(self, u, **k):
        return ('{"summary":"a report","entities":[{"name":"polonium","type":"substance"}],'
                '"relations":[{"src":"polonium","rel":"appears_in","dst":"report"}]}')

with TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    v = Vault(Path(d)/'test.db', offline=True)
    v.add("A scheduled report about polonium.", title="report")
    result = v.connect(chat=_Chat())

    assert result['entities'] > 0
    assert v.search('polonium')
    result
```

## Try it

The cells below use the default embedding model. With `offline=True` the
vault uses `hash_embed` from litesearch. `hash_embed` needs no download
and matches spelling, not meaning. `stats()['encoder']` says which model
is in use.

``` python
      '## Multi-head\n\nHeads attend to different subspaces in parallel.', 'Attention', kind='note')
v.stats()
```

``` python
test_eq(v.stats()['docs'], 2)
test_eq(v.stats()['encoder'], 'model2vec')
assert v.search('chunking')[0]['snippet']
# a hit is a handle plus enough text to recognise it, not the chunk itself; the scoring
# internals the two legs disagree about (`rank`, `_dist`, `_rrf_score`, `rowid`) stay inside
_h = v.search('chunking')[0]
test_eq(sorted(_h), ['age', 'breadcrumb', 'doc_id', 'node_id', 'page', 'score', 'snippet', 'stale'])
assert len(v.search('chunking', chars=20)[0]['snippet']) <= 20
assert v.read(_h['node_id'])['text']          # the handle opens what the snippet came from
test_eq([d['kind'] for d in v.sources()], ['note', 'note'])
test_eq(len(v.sources(kind='web')), 0)
test_eq(len(v.search('chunking', kind='web')), 0)
```

``` python
d = v.doc('Attention')                          # by title substring
test_eq(v.doc(d['id'])['title'], 'Attention')   # by doc_id
test_eq(v.doc(d['source'])['title'], 'Attention')  # by source
test_eq(v.doc('nothing in here'), None)

whole = v.document('Attention')
test_eq((whole.origin, whole.nodes), ('vault', 3))   # the root, the heading, the subheading
# every section, in document order, with the headings that say what each one is
assert whole.text.index('Scaled dot-product') < whole.text.index('## Multi-head') < whole.text.index('subspaces')
test_eq(v.document('Attention', headings=False).text.find('## Multi-head'), -1)
test_eq(v.document('Attention', max_chars=20).text, whole.text[:20])
test_eq(v.document('Attention', max_chars=20).truncated, True)
# a `Pages n–m:` node title is build_tree's placeholder, not a heading the document wrote
v.add('Prose with no headings at all, long enough to chunk and to be stored in the vault.', 'plain')
assert '# Pages' not in v.document('plain').text and 'Prose with no' in v.document('plain').text

test_eq(v.set_meta(d['id'], doctype='paper')['doctype'], 'paper')
test_eq(v.doc(d['id'])['meta']['doctype'], 'paper')                 # survives the round trip
test_eq(v.set_meta(d['id'], reviewed=True)['doctype'], 'paper')     # merged, not replaced
test_fail(lambda: v.document('no such document'), contains='no document in the vault')
```

``` python
test_eq(tidy_bc('Attention › Pages 1–1: Scaled dot-product › Multi-head'), 'Attention › Multi-head')
test_eq(tidy_bc(None), '')
```

``` python
from functools import partial
from vishalakshi.ask import CHAT_CACHE, CachedChat, use_chat
```

``` python
# the extraction replays from recordings, so the tests run without the model; VISHALAKSHI_RECORD_CHAT=1 records a miss
with use_chat(partial(CachedChat, path=CHAT_CACHE)): r = v.connect()
assert r['entities'] > 0
# `entities` is what each batch wrote and `merged` what resolution folded away again, so the rows
# left are the difference: one batch covers a corpus this size, and stats counts no topic node
test_eq(v.stats()['entities'], r['entities'] - r['merged'])
```
